items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: We did not see him as we were in tourist class and he was in first class.

ctx.x: The fellows in my group left Algiers the 14th for France. Lily and I left for Morocco the following day. Omar drove us to the airport and the Meltons met us there. Our flight was for 4:10 that afternoon. We had drinks with the Meltons and Omar while waiting for our flights to be announced. This, we never heard, and the Meltons were obliged to leave as their children had gone to see a movie and were to be met by their parents about 4'30. We asked at the entrance of the waiting room if our flight had been called…

An hour after we boarded the plane, it had not moved an inch, and everybody was beginning to get nervous. Then there was an announcement that the plane was waiting for an Ethiopian Minister or something. It was six o'clock when this big shot arrived. We did not see him as we were in tourist class and he was in first class.

Soft music was playing during the time we were waiting. When it was announced that this minister has arrived, and the plane would take off, people started whistling, which has the same meaning as booing. The music immediately became very loud in order to try to keep this fellow from hearing the whistling of dissatisfied people, bit I am certain that he heard it.
